name: Tikrit
summary: A city on the Tigris remembered as the birthplace of Saladin.
overview: Tikrit stood on the Tigris in the broader political world of the medieval Middle East.
Although outside Europe, it is included here because Saladin's career directly shaped crusading history and medieval European politics.

imageInfo.caption: A silver dirham struck at the Tikrit mint about 1009–1010 for the Uqaylid ruler Muzahir al-Dawla — a medieval object naming the Tigris town where Saladin was born in 1137/38.
imageInfo.creator: Photograph of a medieval coin (uploader unattributed)
imageInfo.note: No photograph of medieval Tikrit survives, and little medieval fabric is left on the site; this contemporary coin, minted in the town itself, is honest on-period evidence of Tikrit in the century before Saladin's birth there.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Tikrit is a city on the Tigris in northern Mesopotamia associated with the family of Saladin. Saladin was born there around 1137 while his father Najm ad-Din Ayyub served as its governor.
The city sits on an important river crossing and was part of the contested frontier zone between Abbasid and Seljuk spheres of control in the twelfth century.

contentSections.title: Historical significance
paragraphs: Saladin's family — the Ayyubids — were Kurdish military commanders who rose through Zengid service. His father and uncle Shirkuh both served Imad ad-Din Zengi and Nur ad-Din before Saladin's own rise to prominence in Egypt.
Tikrit represents the provincial military world of the Jazira (Upper Mesopotamia) that produced the commanders who eventually countered crusader power in the late twelfth century.
